standard_prerequisites.name: The ideal of an adically complete pair is contained in the Jacobson radical
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-radical-completion}, cited at proof lines 2488-2489
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the first half of the henselian property.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting of factorisations of monic polynomials through surjections with locally nilpotent kernels
standard_prerequisites.use: Lifts the factorisation successively modulo the powers of the ideal.

core_obligations: Show the ideal lies in the Jacobson radical (proof lines 2488-2489).
Take a monic polynomial with a factorisation of its reduction generating the unit ideal (proof lines 2490-2493).
Lift the factorisation successively modulo the powers of the ideal (proof lines 2494-2496).
Pass to the limit, using that the ring is the inverse limit of the quotients by those powers (proof lines 2497-2499).
proof_roadmap: Successive lifting of the factorisation (proof lines 2490-2496).
Limit gives the factorisation over the ring (proof lines 2497-2499).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a pair whose ring is complete with respect to the ideal is henselian. The proof checks the defining lifting property for factorisations of monic polynomials: the ideal is contained in the Jacobson radical by the standard result on complete rings, and a factorisation of the reduction modulo the ideal is lifted successively modulo the powers of the ideal using the locally nilpotent lifting result, which is legitimate because the quotients by successive powers form a system with locally nilpotent kernels. Since the ring is the inverse limit of those quotients, the compatible system of lifts produces a factorisation over the ring itself.
